plan.notes: University of Denver is on the quarter system (Fall/Winter/Spring); term_system=quarter. Official sample 4-year course plan from the 2025-2026 Undergraduate Bulletin Public Policy program PDF (12 quarters). VARIABLE-CREDIT RECONCILIATION: the bulletin lists ABRE 2988 (study-abroad resident credit) as 0-18 credits and declares 'Total Credits: 174-192'. ABRE 2988 is encoded at 16 (the typical DU study-abroad quarter, cf. the economics/sociology/finance plans), which reconciles the Third Year Fall term total to within the bulletin's stated 0-18 and yields a degree total of 190, inside the bulletin's declared 174-192. ANOMALY DOCUMENTED: the bulletin prints NO credit value for the 'PPOL Specialization' slot in Second Year Fall; its own term total (12 = 4+4+4) and degree range (174-192, exactly explained by ABRE 2988 alone) confirm it contributes 0 to the bulletin's arithmetic. It is encoded as a 0-credit choice slot with this documentation — no value invented. Declared total 190 = plan's actual sum; term totals (Y1 16/16/16, Y2 12/16/18, Y3 16/16/16, Y4 16/16/16) reconcile exactly with the bulletin's stated values. Generic slots (Common Curriculum/SI sequences, minor/elective blocks, PPOL specialization/elective slots, ASEM, study-abroad block) encoded as choice slots exactly as the official plan lists them; no courses invented. BA requires 183 credits for the degree; public policy major requires 44 credits (required core: PPOL 1910, 2000, 2450, 2460, 3115, 3300, plus a 12-credit specialization of three classes within one of five standing specializations or an advisor-approved unique one). Footnote 1: INTZ 2501 Exploring Global Citizenship is required for any student who studies abroad and may be taken in any quarter within the year prior to studying abroad.
